name: Bellhop Redis store behaviour
description: The behaviour specific to the Redis store and Redis-compatible servers: server detection, durability and eviction warnings, recovery from a flush or reset, capability reporting, ShardByQueue scope and hybrid notifications. The command set, data model, Lua rules, topologies and server versions are technical specifications (TECH-52 to TECH-87).

entities.name: RedisStore
entities.description: The Redis store as seen by one node.

ears.when: the connection is established and a trivial EVAL script succeeds
ears.shall: identify the server family and version from HELLO and INFO, apply that family's adjustments, mark the store ready and show the family and version in the startup summary

requirements.notes: Valkey reports redis_version 7.2.4 in INFO, so detection must use HELLO (RDV-1). Families: Redis, Valkey, Garnet, Dragonfly, Kvrocks, KeyDB, Redict, unknown.

ears.when: the connection is established and a trivial EVAL script succeeds
ears.if: the server family is not recognised
ears.shall: log a warning that names what was detected and continue

requirements.notes: Same event as REQ-500 with an extra consequence.

sources.quote: An unknown family is allowed with a warning

ears.while: a node using the Redis store is starting
ears.if: the server does not support EVAL
ears.shall: stop the node from starting with a message that names the server flag that enables scripting, such as --lua on Garnet

sources.quote: a missing EVAL is a startup failure with a message naming the server flag to enable it

ears.if: INFO persistence shows that AOF is off, or the server persists by snapshot only
ears.shall: log a warning that acknowledged jobs can be lost in a crash, naming the server's durability flag where one exists, such as --aof-commit-wait on Garnet

requirements.notes: If INFO persistence is not available on the server, the source says 'where available'; what to log then is open.

ears.shall: log a notice that replication is asynchronous and a failover can drop acknowledged writes

ears.if: maxmemory-policy is anything other than noeviction
ears.shall: log a warning that the server may evict job data
include the persistence mode in the health check and report used_memory against maxmemory

requirements.notes: used_memory reporting is SHOULD (RED-13); the persistence mode is MUST (RED-7). Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: the check turns Degraded above 80% of maxmemory (REQ-519, REQ-520).

ears.when: the generation marker key is found missing
ears.shall: log the ERROR event StoreWasReset and start re-seeding the code-defined recurring jobs and the queue registry

requirements.notes: Causes: FLUSHALL, eviction, restore from an old snapshot. Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: a run whose job record vanished in the reset writes back a minimal record when it completes (REQ-521) and its heartbeats are ignored meanwhile (REQ-522). Runtime-defined recurring jobs cannot be re-seeded; the loss is reported and health stays Degraded until an operator acknowledges it (REQ-523 to REQ-525).

ears.while: the Redis store is reconciling after a reset
ears.shall: report the node Degraded

sources.quote: the health check turns degraded until reconciliation completes

ears.when: the code-defined recurring jobs and the queue registry have been re-seeded
ears.shall: write a new generation marker and mark the store ready

requirements.notes: Writing a new marker is implied; without it the reset would be detected again on the next check.

ears.when: RecurringReconcileInterval, 5 minutes by default, has passed since the last reconciliation
ears.shall: reconcile the code-defined recurring jobs again so that a flush never silently stops them

ears.while: the generation marker is missing and a node is running
ears.shall: eventually re-seed every code-defined recurring job

sources.quote: a flush never silently stops them

ears.where: the server runs standalone, as primary and replica with Sentinel, or as a Cluster
ears.shall: start and run without refusing the topology

requirements.rationale: Correctness comes from one atomic script per transition (TECH-57), not from refusing to start.

sources.quote: The store MUST NOT fail closed on a topology it recognises

ears.shall: enforce unique keys per queue rather than per namespace

requirements.notes: This weakens INV-100: two active jobs with the same unique key can exist in different queues.

sources.quote: in that mode uniqueness scope is per queue

ears.shall: report in the Redis store's capability set no transactional enqueue, while offering push notifications and result storage

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: free-text payload search is dropped from Bellhop altogether as overkill; tag filters (BLT-9) cover looking jobs up by business key. Checked against current Redis: pub/sub gives push notifications and hashes with TTLs give result storage on every supported server, while no Redis server can join the application's SQL transaction. Redis 8 does ship a query engine with full-text search, but it is not used (RDV-2).

ears.shall: lower the default payload hard limit to 256 KB on the Redis store
cap the size of captured logs and job results and give them a TTL

requirements.notes: The TTL value is not given. It must not be shorter than the job's own retention, or INV-119 breaks.

ears.when: a node has not sent a heartbeat for longer than the stale-node age
ears.shall: remove its node registration

requirements.notes: The stale-node age is not given.

ears.where: UseRedisNotifications() pairs a SQL store with Redis
ears.shall: publish a wake-up signal on Redis so other nodes pick up work without waiting for the next poll

ears.where: UseRedisNotifications() pairs a SQL store with Redis
ears.shall: keep processing by polling the SQL store at PollInterval

sources.quote: if it is unavailable the SQL store falls back to polling

ears.where: UseRedisNotifications() pairs a SQL store with Redis
ears.shall: never read job state from Redis; the SQL store is the only source of truth

sources.quote: Redis is then a signal, never a source of truth

ears.shall: not test or document Tendis, Pika/PikiwiDB or other region-specific forks, but accept reports about them

ears.if: the Redis server's used_memory is above RedisMemoryDegradedShare of its maxmemory
ears.shall: report the node Degraded

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: an eviction is a store reset in disguise, so warn early.

ears.shall: default RedisMemoryDegradedShare to 80% (RedisMemoryDegradedShare)

ears.when: a run completes or fails and its job's record no longer exists because the store's generation changed since the claim
ears.shall: write a minimal job record with the job's id, name, outcome and node, marked as recreated after a store reset, and log a warning

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06 so the outcome is not lost from history. This is not a stale token in the sense of jobs INV-128: there is no current record to protect. A record missing for any other reason is still refused.

ears.if: a heartbeat or progress write finds its job's record missing because the store's generation changed since the claim
ears.shall: ignore the write without error and let the run continue

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06; the run's result is recorded at completion (REQ-521).

ears.shall: log an ERROR saying that runtime-defined recurring jobs may have been lost and cannot be re-seeded, and record the reset as unacknowledged

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: report only; nodes do not cache runtime definitions.

ears.if: a store reset has not been acknowledged
ears.shall: report the node Degraded

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06. Lasts beyond reconciliation (REQ-508), until an operator acknowledges the reset (REQ-525).

ears.when: an operator acknowledges a store reset on the dashboard
ears.shall: record the reset as acknowledged

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06. Acknowledging is an operate action (dashboard INV-301).

scenarios.title: FLUSHALL is detected and recurring jobs come back
scenarios.given: The Redis store is ready with code-defined recurring job nightly-cleanup; someone runs FLUSHALL.
scenarios.then: nightly-cleanup exists again, a new generation marker is written, the store is Ready, one ERROR StoreWasReset event and one ERROR about possibly lost runtime-defined recurring jobs were logged, and health stays Degraded until an operator acknowledges the reset.

scenarios.title: Hybrid notifications survive a Redis outage
scenarios.given: SQL Server store with UseRedisNotifications(); Redis goes down; a job is enqueued on node A.
scenarios.then: Node B picks up the job within PollInterval by polling SQL Server, and no job state was read from Redis.

glossary.generationMarker: A key the store writes so it can tell when its data has been flushed, evicted or restored (REQ-507).
glossary.RedisMemoryDegradedShare: Share of maxmemory above which health reports Degraded; 80% by default (REQ-520).
glossary.ShardByQueue: Opt-in Cluster mode with one hash tag per queue instead of per namespace (INV-500).
